exercise.name: Rocky Pull-up Pulldown

reference.title: Rocky Pull-up Pulldown
reference.listing: Video (movement reference only; the page could not be read at authoring time, so the movement is taken from the exercise name and standard coaching practice)
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

exercise.mechanics: Compound (shoulder adduction and extension, scapular depression and retraction, elbow flexion)
exercise.laterality: Bilateral (one rep in front of the bar, one behind the neck in each loop)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out on each pull, breathe in on the way down.

prescription.tempo: About 1.2 s up, brief hold, 2 s down
prescription.progression: More pairs, then a slower lowering

cues.text: Hang from the bar with a wide overhand grip, arms straight.
Pull the shoulder blades down first.
Pull up in front of the bar: chest toward it, elbows down and back.
Chin over the bar, neck long.
Lower under control to the full hang.
Now pull up behind the bar: head forward a little, elbows straight down by the sides.
Bar level with the back of the neck; do not let it hit the head or neck.
Full hang, then the next pair.

mistakes.mistake: Yanking the head forward for the behind-the-neck rep
mistakes.fix: Tilt the head only slightly; the body moves forward under the bar.
Stop with the bar at the base of the neck, a few cm away.
Keep the legs quiet; pull with the back.
Return to straight arms between reps.

mistakes.mistake: Forcing the back rep with stiff shoulders
mistakes.fix: Skip the behind-the-neck rep if you cannot get there without pain.

kinematics.peak: ≈133° (front) and ≈140° (behind the neck) at the top
kinematics.norm: Nearly straight in the hang to well bent at the top of both reps (common coaching standard; elbow range as in Youdas 2010)

kinematics.setup: Overhand, grip points 64 cm apart (shoulder joints 39 cm): about 164% of shoulder width
Chin 51 cm below the bar in the hang
kinematics.peak: Front rep: chin 1.8 cm above the bar
kinematics.norm: Front rep: chin over the bar (common standard for a full rep)

kinematics.setup: Body moves forward under the bar as the pull starts
kinematics.peak: Bar behind the head, base of the neck (C7) 4.7 cm below it; head tilted 16° forward
kinematics.norm: Back rep: bar level with the base of the neck, head slightly forward (common coaching standard); behind-the-neck pulling needs good shoulder mobility (clinical opinion)

kinematics.peak: About 1.2 s up, 0.4 s hold, 1.9 s down for each rep
kinematics.norm: About 1.2 s up and 2 s down (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual 16053, Rocky Pull-up Pulldown, video (movement reference)
Youdas et al. 2010, surface EMG activation patterns and elbow joint motion during a pull-up, chin-up, or perfect-pullup rotational exercise (J Strength Cond Res 24(12):3404-3414)
Signorile, Zink & Szwed 2002, a comparative electromyographical investigation of muscle utilization patterns using various hand positions during the lat pull-down (J Strength Cond Res 16(4):539-546)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness, tingling or giving-way occurs.
Check the bar is secure and can take your weight before hanging from it.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
The behind-the-neck rep puts the shoulder in wide abduction and outward rotation: skip it if you have shoulder pain, instability or limited mobility.
Never let the bar touch the neck or head.
Step or drop down from the bar with control; do not let go at the top.
progressions: Pause at the top of each rep.
